items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was on the same program with Ruth Brown. I found out that he could speak as well as he could perform on the instrument... When he introduced Ruth Brown, he said, 'Ladies and gentlemen, at this time it’s with a great deal of pleasure that I present to you the eminent and inimitable' ... Ruth Brown

ctx.x: This is some inside stuff [laughs]. Yes, she’s a good singer. She let me know that Bird was coming to town. She was practically a Bird groupie [laughs], if such a term can be applied. I think we were together. We went to hear Bird. I of course had heard his recordings and was happily impressed with his live appearance. I was also

impressed with his microphone technique. He was on the same program with Ruth Brown. I found out that he could speak as well as he could perform on the instrument, and I gained a new respect for him then. My next experience with Bird was my first night in New York City to join the Count Basie orchestra, Monday, July 27, 1953. I don’t remember too many dates. I remember the day, the date and the year. items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: You know Ruth? We were talking with Ruth

ctx.x: I think there’s a big part of teaching that’s sometimes left out is just dealing with hearing and playing something from in here where, instead of off a sheet of paper.

You know Ruth? We were talking with Ruth and basically what she said was when you play these notes, these notes are expensive. The notes cost you something. You know there’s an emotional price tag to those notes.
